$comment: Sync state for every upstream Ori Studio ports or bundles. Consolidates four
pins that previously lived in four different places and formats.
Two commits are tracked per upstream and they mean different things:
vendored_commit     what third_party/<name>/ actually contains, and what
the parity oracle compiles against. Moves only on a
real re-vendor, never by a drift check.
last_checked_commit how far a drift check has triaged. Moves every run,
whether or not it found work.
Drift checks are run with the upstream-drift skill; see
reference-finder is not a port: its vendored C++ is compiled to wasm by
scripts/build-reference-finder.mjs and consumed as a black box, so its
port_map names the build recipe rather than Rust files, and its oracle is a
build-equivalence check (from-source wasm vs upstream's committed artifact),
TreeMaker 5.0.1 is absent on purpose: the upstream is a 2015 release and

unported_upstream_features: Apollonius circle drawing tools (MouseHandlerCircleDrawApollonius, MouseHandlerCircleDrawApolloniusRadius), added upstream in PR #505. Vendored but not ported: a product decision about whether Ori Studio wants the tool, not a parity gap.

box-pleating-studio.vendored_commit_note: First commit-level pin for this upstream. The previous pin was derived from the vendored package.json version 0.7.14 resolved to its release tag, and confirmed exact: the vendored tree matched that tag file-for-file before the bump to v0.7.15.
open_port_candidates: roughContour.ts stale-contour clear (v0.7.15). May not apply: our layout/contours.rs computes into a fresh result map rather than mutating persistent node state. See implementation-plans/bp-studio-sync-2026-08-10.md.

flat-folder.vendored_subset_note: Unlike the other upstreams this is a curated subset, not a full copy: 20 files, with large images and the upstream example corpus deliberately omitted. A re-vendor must update the vendored files rather than copying the tree.

origami-simulator.vendored_path_note: Not vendored. packages/origami-simulator is a TypeScript port and a WebGL2 modernization, not a copy; the source commit is recorded in its NOTICE file.

reference-finder.vendored_commit_note: package.json version 4.8.1, subject 'Update names', 2026-08-20. This pin is what scripts/build-reference-finder.mjs compiles to wasm, what its dev-only fallback fetch of upstream's committed src/lib/ref.{js,wasm} is SHA-verified against, and what the build-equivalence oracle compares the from-source build to.
reference-finder.vendored_subset_note: Curated subset like flat-folder, not a full copy: src/core/** (the engine and its Emscripten interop), makefile (the authoritative compiler-flag list; never invoked directly, the build script copies its flags), LICENSE, package.json (the only file stating a GPL version), README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, .clang-format, .clang-tidy. Omitted on purpose: the React app (src/app), locales, icons, public assets, pnpm-lock.yaml, the rsbuild/eslint/gulp configuration, and upstream's committed build outputs src/lib/ref.{js,wasm}, which are rebuilt from src/core into the gitignored apps/web/src/generated/reference-finder/ so no binary is tracked. A re-vendor must update the vendored files rather than copying the tree.

local_patches.note: Search patch (README.treemaker.md, 'Local changes'): FindBestMarks/FindBestLines score every basis reference once per query from per-database caches (line paper clips, ranks) instead of recomputing DistanceTo for both operands of every comparison. Bit-identical answers, ~13x faster line queries. A re-vendor re-applies it on top of the new pin and re-runs tools/reference-finder-oracle/equiv.mjs, whose queries.json covers every search setting the app uses. Not upstreamed on purpose: upstream shows one solution per query and does not feel the cost.

reference-finder.port_map_note: Nothing is ported. The only mapping is the build recipe: scripts/build-reference-finder.mjs copies the makefile's flags and must be re-read on every makefile change. Changes under src/core/ are consumed by re-vendoring and rebuilding, not by porting.
